Material applications, support contrast, default interior information and the A palette agree with the upstream specification and materials sheet.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Use the coordinate convention x=0 at the front, positive y toward the boarding side and z=0 at the road. Drawings must respect body sides y=±1100; axle centres x=1400 and 5400; four wheel centres at y=±850, z=325; interior width y=-1000 to 1000; passenger floor x=1800–6500 at z=320; and ceiling z=2700. Preserve the driver-control zone x=250–1750, y=-1000 to 0 and its existing controls. Treat wheelhouses at x=1050–1750 and 5050–5750, side bands y=-1000 to -650 and 650–1000, z=320–700, and the rear service volume x=6500–6850, y=-1000 to 1000, z=320–850 as solid. The main aisle remains x=1800–6500, y=-250 to 500. Locate the landing at x=1900–3100, y=-250 to 1000 and provide doorway height 2100 above the passenger floor. The bridge spans x=1950–3050, deploys from y=1100, z=320 to y=1800, z=300, and fits its stow allowance x=1950–3050, y=350–1100, z=100–300. Door leaves and motion may be designed freely within these constraints. Paired state drawings must show a usable open/deployed arrangement and a credible closed/stowed arrangement. Dimension labels, sections and consistent drawing geometry count as evidence; conflicting geometry or intrusion into required clear regions fails.

Neutral technical plans, elevations and sections are permitted when their intended colourway is identified; they do not need rendered palette fills. This exception does not replace the palette requirements for coloured renderings or swatches.

The process specification must provide a usable upstream record of chassis coordinates and reserved volumes, fixed and tip-up seat use envelopes, N8/F6 labels and passenger counts, doorway/landing/bridge geometry, open/deployed and closed/stowed mechanism states, stopped-vehicle service order, physical controls, support dimensions and contrast, installed fixed copy, route records, and part-to-material assignments. Values must agree with the client fact sheet. Body panels, lining and support finishes require explicit proposed assignments; upholstery and flooring retain their fixed materials. A generic design narrative, unresolved assignments or contradictory records fails. File content establishes the specification's source role; export chronology is not inferred from appearance.

Read a labelled specification for A with base #E8E6DD and accent #1A655E, and B with the same base and accent #655168. Identify body-panel, lining, support-finish, seat-cover and floor assignments that agree with the upstream specification, including recycled PET upholstery and nonslip rubber flooring. State support-to-background LRV difference of at least 30 points. Body and lining material choices, support finishes and accent placement are open, but assignments must remain shared across A/B. Missing codes, an unspecified material category, changed fixed materials or contradictory assignments fails.

The exterior orthographic sheet and passenger layout must each visibly repeat the specification's 4000 mm wheelbase and 1200 mm clear doorway width. Label both modes on the paired layout and the appropriate mode on each corresponding interior image: N8 on the N8 view and F6 on the F6 view. Matching values located elsewhere in the submission do not satisfy a missing required annotation on these sheets; conflicting values or mislabelled states fail.

All views must describe one body with the stated envelope, wheel size and right-side doorway position. The layout must label/count eight passenger seats in N8 and six in F6, excluding the driver, and individually identify T1/T2. Dimension aisle 750 mm, landing 1200 by 1250 mm, stroller space 1000 by 600 mm, separate caregiver space 500 by 500 mm and folded projections no greater than 120 mm. Six fixed seats comprise three per side: two complete use envelopes per side inside x=3500–5000 and one inside x=5800–6500, in the prescribed side bands; each envelope is at least 700 by 450 mm. Two separate deployed tip-up envelopes of 600 by 750 mm fit within F at x=1800–3500, y=-1000 to -250. In F6 both seats fold and the longitudinal stroller and caregiver envelopes fit within F clear of each other, folded seats and aisle. Include open/deployed and closed/stowed door/bridge states. Viewpoint variation is permitted; altered hard points, missing dimensions, seat-count errors or conflicting occupancy fails.

Material labels and visible applications must agree with the specification's part assignments, including recycled PET seat fabric and nonslip rubber flooring. The facilities sheet must contain door and flexible-bay sections, dimensioned positions for physical STOP buttons, rail diameter 35 mm and adjacent-surface clearance 38 mm. Explicitly state support-to-background LRV difference of at least 30 points. Show doorway/interior grasp points and bay support/retention equipment installed without obstructing the aisle, doorway, landing or required passenger envelopes; boundary contact is permitted. Locate LET PASSENGERS EXIT FIRST at the door and FOLD BOTH SEATS BEFORE STROLLER PARKING at the bay. A loose legend, unlocated controls, missing placement dimensions, substituted fixed materials or incompatible installations fails.

All three sheets must use S1, Library forecourt, R1, with N8 for E1/E3 and F6 for E2. Number the stationary sequence through waiting outside, opening the door, deploying the bridge, clearing exiting passengers, boarding, stowing the bridge after passage clears and closing the door. E1 reaches an already deployed near-door tip-up via visible supports. E2 starts with both tip-ups folded and demonstrates entry, turning and parking with separate caregiver space and clear aisle. E3 includes an alighting passenger and a waiting passenger beyond the bridge path. Each sheet must dimension floor 320 mm, curb 300 mm, gap 100 mm and bridge width/reach 1100 by 700 mm; the bridge descends 20 mm over its reach. Preserve the stop landing x=1700–3500, y=1200–3000, curb edge y=1200, and submitted door, seat and support positions. Temporary passage through clear regions is allowed, and walking aids or stroller occupants are optional; incorrect case records, conflicting hardware, obstructed final parking or unsafe ordering fails.

Review the entire film and its duration: it must run 12 seconds and include both an exterior observation and E2 caregiver/stroller boarding at S1 Library forecourt on R1. The A vehicle remains stationary in every shot and agrees with the submitted body, F6 seating, installed supports and warm-white/teal palette. T1/T2 are folded before entry. Show waiting, door opening, bridge deployment, exiting passengers clearing, boarding with entry/turning/parking, bridge stowage after passage clears and door closure in that order. Final stroller and caregiver positions remain separate and clear of the aisle. Visible identification and route information must retain the default records. Editing and camera movement are permitted; omitted operations, wrong duration, vehicle motion, inconsistent hardware or boarding before exit clearance fails.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: Every image sheet title must contain NEARLINK. Front and boarding-side identification, wherever those surfaces are shown, must pair the name with three vertically stacked open circles linked by a straight vertical spine. Read exterior displays as R1 / MARKET and interior information as NEXT STOP / POOL with the complete Library → Pool → Market strip. Coloured vehicle views must implement A's #E8E6DD base and #1A655E accent consistently with the materials sheet, which also identifies B's #655168 accent. Do not require hidden surfaces to become visible or literal hex-matched pixels under dusk lighting; missing required information, wrong stop order, changed symbol structure or a substituted palette fails.

The overview must include front, right-side and rear orthographic views and a front-right perspective; the rear-left role must show that distinct viewpoint; the dusk role must establish dusk lighting with the passenger door closed and bridge fully stowed. All depict A/R1 with finished contemporary surfacing, glazing and considered lighting within the fixed envelope. Composition may vary, but missing view types, duplicate viewpoints substituted for required coverage or a deployed bridge in the dusk view fails.

Provide readable A interiors for both operating modes. The N8 view shows six fixed seats and both tip-ups deployed, without a parked stroller; the F6 view shows the same fixed seating with both tip-ups folded and both stroller and separate caregiver spaces occupied. Camera choice may vary, but the near-door state and preserved aisle must be visible enough to verify against the layout. A stroller occupant is optional. Empty F6 spaces, ambiguous tip-up states or moved seating/support installations fails.

The presentation must have at least eight pages and a cover bearing NEARLINK. Beside the applicable vehicle and layout work, state wheelbase 4000 mm and doorway width 1200 mm. Identify N8 with eight passenger seats and F6 with six, and associate A with #E8E6DD/#1A655E and B with #E8E6DD/#655168. Records must agree with the specification and materials sheet. Page count above the minimum and flexible page organisation are allowed; missing adjacent facts, wrong seat totals, incomplete colour codes or a missing cover name fails.

Locate recognisable reuse from every listed source, including readable specification records, both colourway specifications, each exterior and interior view, layout, facilities and all three case sequences. Scaling, cropping and rearrangement are acceptable when the original work remains identifiable and its relevant evidence remains readable. Merely naming a source, replacing it with a newly inconsistent design or omitting any source role fails.

All exterior directions and lighting conditions retain one body, glazing, lamp, door and identification design consistent with the specification. The exterior family applies the materials sheet's A palette and default R1 information; the dusk state closes the door and stows the bridge.

Plans, perspectives and installation sections preserve the same six fixed seats, identifiable tip-ups, clear regions and installed controls across the two service states. Material applications, support contrast, default interior information and the A palette agree with the upstream specification and materials sheet.

Passenger sequences use the submitted vehicle and installed geometry, preserving component positions while changing only passenger action and the prescribed mechanism states. E1–E3 share the recorded stationary S1/R1 boarding interface and exit-first service order while retaining their distinct N8/F6 actions.
